properties.summary: Ligand fluorescence and weak, rapidly decaying emission tentatively assigned to Eu(II) were observed. The Eu(III) luminescence is attributed to an oxidation impurity, not the Eu(II) polymer.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Eight-coordinate Eu(II) centers in edge-linked square-antiprismatic polyhedra form chains through bridging trifluoroacetate and DMF ligands.

synthesis.procedure: Under argon, Eu metal was dissolved in dried liquid ammonia and ammonium trifluoroacetate was added. The yellow suspension was stirred at approximately −30 °C for 1 h. After evaporation and vacuum drying, a portion of the crude powder was stirred with DMF; the clear solution was concentrated and stored in a sealed ampoule at 8 °C.
synthesis.temperature: Approximately −30 °C for the initial reaction; 8 °C for crystallization
synthesis.time: 1 h stirring; insoluble material settled overnight; crystals grew within 1–2 weeks
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Reaction vessel with glass-coated stir bar; sealed ampoule for crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Ammonia was evaporated; residue was dried under vacuum for 8 h to 10−3 hPa and ground. The DMF supernatant was transferred, concentrated to half-volume under vacuum, and cooled. Yellow needles were dried under vacuum to 5 × 10−3 hPa.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Six Eu(III) ions form an octahedron with eight fluoride-capped faces. Twelve bridging trifluoroacetates span its edges, and six coordinated trifluoroacetic acid molecules occupy the vertices; two ammonium ions balance the dianionic cluster.

synthesis.procedure: The crude europium–trifluoroacetate product was prepared from Eu metal and ammonium trifluoroacetate in dried liquid ammonia as described for 1. A 150 mg portion was crystallized by the procedure for 1, substituting anhydrous trifluoroacetic acid for DMF.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The Eu6F8 octahedral core has the same face-capping fluoride, edge-bridging carboxylate and vertex-bound acid arrangement as 2, with pentafluoropropionate in place of trifluoroacetate. Eight additional pentafluoropropionic acid molecules lie outside the cluster in hydrogen-bonded layer-like regions, including acid dimers.

synthesis.procedure: Pentafluoropropionic acid was prepared by controlled hydration and distillation of its anhydride. The acid was added to dried liquid ammonia, followed by Eu metal. The yellow suspension was stirred at approximately −30 °C for 1 h. After ammonia evaporation and vacuum drying, 230 mg of crude product was crystallized in anhydrous pentafluoropropionic acid using the sealed-ampoule procedure described for 1.

synthesis.vessel_or_method: Microdistillation apparatus for acid preparation; liquid-ammonia reaction vessel with glass-coated stir bar; PTFE-ring-sealed ampoule for crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: The prepared acid was distilled, collecting the 96–97 °C fraction. Ammonia was evaporated, and the residue was vacuum-dried to 10−3 hPa and ground. After crystallization, the mother liquor was removed and crystals were dried under vacuum to 10−2 hPa.
